HPDi Lab

HPDi Lab is led by Jinzhen Wang in the Department of Computer Science at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte. We study high-performance computing and scientific data management, developing efficient methods for data reduction, compression, and data access in parallel and distributed systems. Our research combines system design, performance modeling, and machine learning to manage large scientific datasets and guide compression decisions. Our mission is to reduce the cost of storing, moving, and processing scientific data while preserving the information needed for analysis and discovery.

Research

Data reduction & compression

Compression quality prediction and configuration selection for scientific datasets.

Scientific data management

Progressive retrieval and efficient access to large scientific datasets.

Parallel & distributed systems

Performance modeling and data movement across modern computing and storage systems.

Projects

IEEE Cluster 2026 · IEEE BigData 2024

Compression Quality Prediction

DeepCQ and QualityNet

Jinzhen Wang

Principal Investigator

Biography

Jinzhen Wang

Principal Investigator

I am an Assistant Professor in the Department of Computer Science at UNC Charlotte, where I lead the High-Performance Data Intensive (HPDi) Lab. My research focuses on high-performance computing and scientific data management, with an emphasis on data reduction, compression, and parallel and distributed systems. I received my Ph.D. from the New Jersey Institute of Technology, advised by Qing Liu, and my bachelor's degree from Shandong University. I was a research intern at Los Alamos National Laboratory from 2022 to 2023. I am also affiliated with the High Performance Computing and Systems Lab at UNC Charlotte.

Data reduction and compression, Scientific data management, Parallel and distributed systems
